scenario: 系统要存储大量按时间追加的监控指标，查询通常按时间范围和少量标签筛选。
scenario_en: The system stores many append-only monitoring metrics, and queries usually filter by time range and a few tags.
q: 什么时候该选择时间序列数据库（TSDB）？
q_en: When should you choose a time-series database (TSDB)?
options: 只要数据里有 timestamp 字段就必须用 TSDB
当业务需要强事务和复杂外键约束时
当通用数据库在高写入、时间范围查询、保留策略和压缩上出现真实瓶颈时
当核心需求是跨全部 series 做 Top-K 排序时
why: 决定性约束是通用数据库先撑不住高写入、时间范围查询或保留/压缩需求；仅有 timestamp 字段不构成理由。先用 Postgres/DynamoDB 顶，顶不住再上专用系统。
why_en: A time-series database is worth adopting once a general-purpose database genuinely bottlenecks on write volume, time-range queries, or retention, not just because the data happens to have a timestamp.
whenOtherWins: 如果查询核心是跨海量 series 的全局排序或强事务/复杂 join，Postgres/DynamoDB 等通用方案通常更直接。
tradeoff: 专用 TSDB 的写入/压缩优化 vs 通用数据库的事务与关系能力
options_en: Any time your data has a timestamp field, you must use a TSDB.
When the business needs strong transactions and complex foreign keys.
When a general-purpose database hits real bottlenecks on high write volume, time-range queries, retention, and compression.
When the core need is Top-K ranking across all series.

scenario_en: A cloud monitoring system has 100,000 servers, each reporting 5 metrics every 10 seconds, which is about 50,000 points per second and 4.3 billion points per day.
q: 这个写入量级对存储引擎的设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does this write scale imply for the storage engine design?
options: 这个量级下单机 Postgres 加两个索引就能长期稳定支撑，不需要改变写入方式
这个量级只影响读延迟，写入可以随意排队，不需要特别设计
这个量级下随机原地更新和逐行索引维护会撑不住，写路径必须转向顺序追加和批量整理
只要磁盘足够大，这个量级对存储引擎设计没有实质影响
why: 50,000 点/秒、一天 43 亿点意味着随机 I/O 和逐行索引会先被拖垮；这正是 append-only + LSM 这类设计存在的原因。
why_en: At roughly 50,000 points per second and 4.3 billion points a day, random I/O and per-row indexing become the bottleneck, which is exactly why append-only and LSM-style engines exist.
options_en: At this scale, a single Postgres instance with two indexes can support it indefinitely without changing how writes work.
At this scale, only read latency is affected, so writes can queue freely without special design.
At this scale, in-place random updates and per-row index maintenance can't keep up, so the write path must shift to sequential appends with batched reorganization.
As long as disks are big enough, this scale has no real effect on storage engine design.

q: 把大规模指标按 timestamp、host、metric_name、value 存到一张普通 Postgres 行式表，会先在哪里出问题？
q_en: Where does a normal Postgres row table first break down for large-scale metrics stored as timestamp, host, metric_name, and value?
options: 只要给 host 和 metric_name 分别建索引，就能同时保证写入吞吐和查询延迟
问题只出现在磁盘空间上，不会影响写入吞吐或查询延迟
标签字符串按行重复存储，加上高写入下的索引维护，会同时拖慢写入并膨胀存储
只要把 value 列类型换成 REAL 而不是 DOUBLE PRECISION 就能解决
why: 决定性约束是每行都重复存 host/metric_name 字符串，且高写入下索引维护很重；加索引或换数据类型都治标不治本。
why_en: The real bottleneck is repeated label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume, which indexing alone or a smaller numeric type can't fix.
options_en: Adding separate indexes on host and metric_name alone is enough to guarantee both write throughput and query latency.
The problem only shows up in disk space; it doesn't affect write throughput or query latency.
Repeating label strings in every row plus heavy index maintenance under high write volume slows writes and bloats storage at the same time.
Switching the value column from DOUBLE PRECISION to REAL is enough to fix it.
codeSample:
CREATE TABLE metrics (
  timestamp TIMESTAMP,
  host VARCHAR(255),
  metric_name VARCHAR(255),
  value DOUBLE PRECISION
);
-- 4.3B rows/day → host+metric_name 反复重复
-- 50k writes/s 起步，索引越加写入越慢

q: Append-only（只追加写）存储的核心思想是什么？
q_en: What is the core idea of append-only storage?
options: 每次写入都先扫描全表
新数据总是追加到文件末尾，避免原地随机更新
只允许删除，不允许写入
每个指标都单独创建数据库
why: 追加写把昂贵的随机 I/O 转成顺序 I/O，特别适合大量持续写入的指标流。代价是之后需要靠 compaction/index 让读取仍然可接受。
why_en: Append-only storage writes new points at the end of files, turning random writes into fast sequential writes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Metric point"] --> B["Memory buffer"]
  B --> C["Append segment"]
  C --> D["Compact later"]
options_en: Every write first scans the entire table.
New data is always appended to the end of a file, avoiding in-place random updates.
Only deletes are allowed, no writes.
Each metric gets its own separate database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在文件末尾追加新数据，不做原地更新的写入方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only storage always writes new data to the end of a file instead of updating in place.

q: 在磁盘 I/O 模式上，append-only 写入相比传统原地更新的优势是什么？
q_en: For disk I/O, what advantage does append-only writing have over traditional in-place updates?
options: 它让每次写入都必须先随机寻址到旧 block 再修改
它省去定位旧数据、读、改、写的步骤，只在文件尾部顺序追加
它保证所有查询都不必再使用任何索引
它只能在纯内存数据库里生效，磁盘数据库用不了
why: 原地更新要先定位旧位置再读改写，产生随机 I/O；append-only 只在文件尾追加，把随机变顺序，代价是空间需要靠后台整理回收。
why_en: In-place updates need to locate, read, modify, and rewrite old data, causing random I/O, while append-only writes sequentially at the end and reclaims space later via background compaction.
tradeoff: 顺序追加换取写入吞吐 vs 原地更新换取即时空间复用
options_en: It forces every write to randomly seek to an old block and modify it first.
It skips locating, reading, modifying, and rewriting old data, appending sequentially at the end of the file instead.
It guarantees every query no longer needs any index.
It only works for pure in-memory databases, not disk-based ones.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对磁盘上分散位置的读写，需要额外寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Random I/O reads or writes scattered disk locations and pays extra seek overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按顺序连续读写磁盘位置，没有寻址开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential I/O reads or writes contiguous disk locations without seek overhead.

scenario: 为高吞吐指标流选型时，需要判断随机写和顺序写在机械硬盘上的量级差异。
scenario_en: When choosing storage for a high-throughput metric stream, you need to judge the order-of-magnitude gap between random and sequential writes on spinning disks.
q: 机械硬盘上，随机 I/O 相比顺序 I/O 的数量级差异大致是什么？
q_en: On spinning disks, roughly how different are random I/O and sequential I/O?
options: 随机 I/O 永远比顺序 I/O 快 100 倍
SSD 无论随机还是顺序都完全一样，二者无差别
机械硬盘随机操作通常只有百级 ops/s，顺序写吞吐可以高出一到两个数量级
磁盘 I/O 模式与数据库写入设计无关
why: 机械硬盘随机操作受限于磁头寻道，通常百级 ops/s；顺序写能到万级甚至更高。这个差距正是 append-only 设计存在的理由。
why_en: Spinning disks are limited to roughly hundreds of random operations per second because of head seeks, while sequential writes can reach far higher throughput, which is exactly why append-only design pays off.
options_en: Random I/O is always 100 times faster than sequential I/O.
SSDs perform identically whether access is random or sequential.
Spinning disks typically manage only hundreds of random ops per second, while sequential writes can be one to two orders of magnitude higher.
Disk I/O pattern has nothing to do with database write design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固态硬盘，没有机械寻道臂，但顺序访问仍比随机访问更友好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSD is flash-based storage with no mechanical seek arm, though sequential access is still friendlier than random access.

q: 把 LSM tree 写入路径按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the LSM tree write path in order:
steps: 后台 compaction 合并多个 SSTable，清理重复数据和 tombstone
新数据先写入内存中的有序 memtable
memtable 满后顺序刷盘成不可变的有序 SSTable
查询时可能需要检查 memtable 和多个磁盘文件
why: LSM 把前台随机写转为内存写和顺序刷盘，再把组织数据的成本放到后台 compaction。读取会承担检查多个文件的成本。
why_en: LSM trees write to a sorted memtable, flush immutable SSTables, compact them in the background, and may check multiple files on reads.
diagram:
flowchart LR
Write[Incoming points] --> Memtable[Sorted memtable]
Memtable --> SSTable[Immutable SSTable]
SSTable --> Compaction[Background compaction]
Compaction --> Larger[Large sorted files]
Query[Query] --> Memtable
Query --> SSTable

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SSTable is the immutable sorted file an LSM tree writes when it flushes memory to disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 中驻留内存的有序缓冲结构，接收最新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: 合并多个存储文件、清理重复和已删除数据的后台过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compaction is the background process that merges storage files and removes stale or deleted data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标记某条数据已删除的占位记录，等 compaction 时才真正清除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tombstone is a marker recording that a value was deleted; it is physically removed only during compaction.

q: LSM（Log-Structured Merge Tree）的 memtable 为什么通常保持有序？
q_en: Why is the memtable in an LSM tree usually kept sorted?
options: 为了让所有写入都必须等待磁盘完成排序后才算成功
为了强制所有查询必须全表扫描，不能走索引
为了把每个 key 随机分散写到不同文件，避免热点
为了刷盘后直接生成有序 SSTable，方便二分查找、范围扫描和后续合并
why: 内存里排序成本低，刷盘时直接顺序写出有序文件；有序文件支持二分查找、范围扫描，也让后台 merge-sort compaction 更高效。
why_en: A sorted memtable flushes into a sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, efficient ranges, and merge-based compaction.
options_en: So that every write must wait for the disk to finish sorting before it's considered successful.
So that every query is forced to do a full scan instead of using an index.
So that each key is randomly scattered across different files to avoid hotspots.
So that flushing produces an already-sorted SSTable, enabling binary search, range scans, and later merge-based compaction.
optionMeanings: 误以为排序是为了拖慢写入确认速度。
误以为有序结构会禁止索引查询。
误以为有序是为了打散 key 分布。
有序 memtable 刷盘后直接是有序 SSTable。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memtable is the in-memory sorted buffer that absorbs the newest writes in an LSM tree.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSM 刷盘后生成的不可变有序文件。

q: LSM tree（日志结构合并树）的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main tradeoff of an LSM tree?
options: 牺牲所有写入能力，换取只读性能
牺牲部分读性能和写放大，换取高写入吞吐
牺牲压缩能力，换取更高空间占用
完全没有任何后台开销，因此性能只受磁盘限制
why: 读可能要查多个 SSTable，compaction 会重写数据产生写放大。它适合高写入场景，而不是所有 workload 的默认答案。
why_en: LSM trees trade some read cost and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
tradeoff: 高写入吞吐 vs 读放大与写放大
options_en: It gives up all write capability in exchange for read-only performance.
It trades some read performance and write amplification for much higher write throughput.
It gives up compression capability in exchange for higher space usage.
It has zero background overhead, so performance is limited only by disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把随机写转成顺序写，再靠后台合并整理数据的存储结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An LSM tree turns random writes into sequential writes and reorganizes data later via background merges.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由于 compaction 反复重写数据，实际磁盘写入量大于逻辑写入量的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means the actual bytes written to disk exceed the logical write size because compaction rewrites data multiple times.

q: 补全 delta encoding 的思想：
q_en: Complete the idea behind delta encoding:
text: Delta encoding 不反复存完整值，而是存相邻值之间的 {{difference}}；时间序列相邻点通常变化小，所以这些 delta 更容易被 {{compressed}}。
why: CPU、内存、流量等指标通常连续且变化平滑，delta 值比原始值小。配合可变长编码能显著降低存储。
why_en: Delta encoding stores differences between adjacent values, which compress well when time-series data changes gradually.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["t1 t2 t3"] --> B["deltas"]
  B --> C["delta of delta"]
  C --> D["compressed block"]
codeSample:
Raw values:     45.2  45.3  45.1  45.4
Delta encoded:  45.2  +0.1  -0.2  +0.3
# 只存差值，差值比原值小很多，更容易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 存相邻值之间的差而不是完整值的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta encoding stores the difference between adjacent values instead of the full value each time.

q: varint（variable-length encoding，变长整数编码）在 TSDB 压缩中解决什么问题？
q_en: What problem does varint, or variable-length encoding, solve in TSDB compression?
options: 让所有字符串自动转换成图片格式存储
强制每条记录都补齐到固定 1MB 大小
让数值小的整数只占 1-2 字节，而不是固定 4/8 字节
让浮点数从此无法用任何方式存储
why: delta 往往是小数值，varint 能让小值占用 1-2 个字节。它放大了 delta encoding 的空间收益。
why_en: Variable-length encoding stores small deltas in fewer bytes instead of always using a fixed-width integer.
options_en: It automatically converts all strings into image format for storage.
It forces every record to pad out to a fixed 1MB size.
It lets small integers take only 1-2 bytes instead of a fixed 4 or 8 bytes.
It makes floating-point numbers impossible to store at all.
codeSample:
varint(1)        = 0x01            (1 byte)
varint(300)      = 0xAC 0x02       (2 bytes)
varint(1000000)  = 0xC0 0x84 0x3D  (3 bytes)
# 值越小，占用字节越少；delta 编码后大多是小数值

termDefinitions.meaning: 变长整数编码，用更少字节表示小数值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Varint is a variable-length integer encoding that stores small numbers in fewer bytes.

q: 时间戳 delta-of-delta（二阶差分）编码为什么对固定采样间隔特别有效？
q_en: Why is timestamp delta-of-delta encoding especially effective for fixed sampling intervals?
options: 因为 timestamp 不能被排序
因为相邻 timestamp 的间隔经常相同，二阶差分大量为 0
因为它会丢弃真实采样时间，只保留序号
因为所有 timestamp 都必须先转成字符串再比较
why: 如果每 10 秒采样一次，timestamp 的 delta 基本恒定，delta-of-delta 接近 0。大量 0 非常容易压缩。
why_en: Delta-of-delta compression works well because regular sampling intervals make second-order timestamp deltas mostly zero.
options_en: Because timestamps cannot be sorted.
Because the interval between adjacent timestamps is often constant, so second-order deltas are mostly zero.
Because it discards the real sample time and keeps only a sequence number.
Because every timestamp must first be converted to a string before comparison.
codeSample:
Raw timestamps:   1000  1010  1020  1030  1040
Deltas:              10    10    10    10
Delta-of-delta:            0     0     0
# 间隔恒定 → 二阶差分几乎全 0 → 极易压缩

termDefinitions.meaning: 对增量再做一次差分的二阶编码，常用于规律采样的时间戳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delta-of-delta encoding takes the difference of deltas, which collapses to near zero for regularly spaced timestamps.

q: TSDB 对浮点值常用 XOR 压缩的直觉是什么？
q_en: What is the intuition behind XOR compression for floating-point values in a TSDB?
options: 浮点数在时间序列里完全无法做任何压缩处理
XOR 运算会把所有数值变成同一个常数输出
XOR 压缩只对文本字符串生效，对浮点数无效
相邻浮点值接近时，XOR 后多数 bit 是 0，只需存差异部分
why: 相邻指标值通常很接近，二进制表示也有大量相同位。XOR 后只保留有意义的差异位，能显著减少空间。
why_en: XOR compression exploits similar adjacent floating-point values because their XOR contains many zero bits.
options_en: Floating-point values in time series can't be compressed at all.
XOR turns all values into the same constant output.
XOR compression only works on text strings, not floats.
When adjacent float values are close, XORing them leaves mostly zero bits, so only the differing part needs to be stored.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用相邻浮点数按位异或后大量为 0 位来压缩数值的技术。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XOR compression exploits the fact that XORing similar adjacent floating-point values leaves mostly zero bits.

scenario: 监控系统每条指标点只有 timestamp 和一个 float，理论上很小，但落到普通行式表后磁盘占用远超预期。
scenario_en: Each monitoring point only has a timestamp and one float, so the raw payload is tiny, but disk usage grows far beyond expectation in a normal row store.
q: 为什么一条普通指标点的原始信息很小，但行式存储仍可能很浪费？
q_en: Why can a normal metric point be tiny in raw form but still waste space in row storage?
options: 因为每条指标都会被数据库自动复制成完整的一段视频文件保存
因为原始数值本身只有十几字节，但每行还反复存 host、metric_name 等标签字符串
因为 timestamp 这个字段本身在磁盘上要占用大约 10MB 空间
因为浮点数类型在关系数据库里天生完全无法进行任何压缩
why: 实际数值部分很小，空间膨胀多来自重复标签和行式元数据。TSDB 通过 series-oriented 存储和压缩减少这种重复。
why_en: The raw timestamp and value are small, but row stores waste space by repeating labels and row metadata for every point.
options_en: Because every point gets automatically duplicated into a full video file by the database.
Because the raw value itself is only a dozen or so bytes, but every row still repeats label strings like host and metric_name.
Because the timestamp field alone takes about 10MB of disk space.
Because floating-point types in relational databases inherently cannot be compressed at all.

q: Time-based partitioning 在 TSDB 中的含义是什么？
q_en: What does time-based partitioning mean in a TSDB?
options: 按用户名哈希把数据随机拆分成数量不受控的表
把所有历史数据永远放进一个不可删除的大文件

tradeoff: 多读几次文件（false positive）vs 绝不漏掉真实数据（no false negative）
options_en: It sometimes misses keys that really exist, producing a false negative.
It guarantees zero error, with neither false positives nor false negatives.

q: Downsampling / rollup 在 TSDB 中解决什么问题？

把时间戳删除，使数据无法按时间查询

只用于加密用户密码

都把可过滤的值映射到包含它的对象集合
两者都完全不支持对多个条件做集合交集
两者都只能运行在浏览器前端环境里，不能用于服务端

q: 查询 region='us-west' AND env='prod' 时，tag index 通常会怎么用？
q_en: How would a tag index usually handle a query like region='us-west' AND env='prod'?
options: 不看任何索引，直接随机读取所有 block 逐个比对
先把 env 这个 tag 从索引里整个删除再查询
只检查 value 字段是否大于 0，忽略两个 tag 条件
分别查两个 tag 各自的 series 集合，再取交集
why: 集合交集能快速得到同时满足多个 tag 条件的 series。之后只需要读取这些 series 对应的 block。
why_en: A multi-tag query intersects the series sets for each tag predicate before reading data blocks.
options_en: Ignore every index and randomly scan every block one by one.
Delete the env tag from the index entirely before querying.
Only check whether the value field is greater than 0, ignoring both tag conditions.
Look up the series set for each tag separately, then intersect the two sets.

region=us-west → [Series1, Series2]

q: 为什么 series-oriented 存储比普通行式表更适合指标查询？
q_en: Why is series-oriented storage better suited to metric queries than a normal row table?
options: 它让所有数据都不再需要保存时间戳字段
它会彻底禁止用户按任何 tag 做过滤查询
同一 series 的点物理上更集中，查询时更少分散读取
它规定整个数据库里每个 series 只能存一条数据
why: 监控查询常围绕某些 host/service/region 的时间范围。把相关点放在连续 block 中，能减少随机读取并提升压缩率。
why_en: Series-oriented storage colocates related points, reducing scattered reads and improving compression for time-range queries.
tradeoff: 同 series 物理集中换取更少分散读取 vs 行式表按插入顺序存储更简单
options_en: It means data no longer needs to store a timestamp field at all.
It completely bans filtering by any tag.
Points from the same series sit closer together physically, so querying it touches fewer scattered reads.
It restricts the whole database to storing only one point per series.

termDefinitions.meaning: measurement 加上一组具体 tag 值构成的一条时间序列。

q: TSDB 查询 mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) 时，为什么通常不需要先把所有点加载到内存？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query like mean(value) GROUP BY time(5m) usually not need to load all points into memory first?
options: 平均值不需要任何输入数据
聚合可以边读取边累积 sum/count/min/max
磁盘会自动返回最终答案
tag index 会直接存所有聚合结果
why: 聚合函数可以流式计算，只保留每个桶的中间状态。这样查询大时间范围时内存压力更可控。
why_en: Aggregations can be streamed by maintaining bucket state such as sum and count as points are read.
options_en: The average requires no input data at all.
Aggregation can accumulate sum, count, min, and max while streaming through the data.
The disk automatically returns the final answer.
The tag index directly stores every aggregation result.
codeSample:
SELECT mean(value) FROM cpu_usage
WHERE host = 'server-1' AND time > now() - 1h
GROUP BY time(5m)
# 引擎边读边维护每个 5m 桶的 sum/count，不必先加载全部点

termDefinitions.meaning: 边读取数据边累积聚合结果，不必先把全部数据加载进内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Streaming aggregation accumulates results as data is read instead of loading everything into memory first.

q: TSDB 查询快的两个 locality 直觉是什么？
q_en: What are the two locality intuitions behind fast TSDB queries?
options: 用户密码局部性和 CSS 局部性
随机分区局部性和全表扫描局部性
只写不读局部性和只读不写局部性
时间局部性和 series 局部性
why: 时间局部性让查询只看相关 partition；series 局部性让同一 tag 组合的数据块集中。两者共同减少磁盘访问。
why_en: Time-series databases exploit both time locality and series locality to minimize disk access.
options_en: Password locality and CSS locality.
Random partition locality and full-table-scan locality.
Write-only locality and read-only locality.
Time locality and series locality.

q: TSDB 中 cardinality 指的是什么？
q_en: What does cardinality mean in a TSDB?
options: 磁盘上文件的权限数量
每秒 CPU 指令数
唯一 tag 组合，也就是 series 的数量
SQL join 的列数
why: series 数量由 measurement 和 tag 组合决定。cardinality 高会让内存 tag index 和元数据膨胀。
why_en: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, or series, that the database must track.
options_en: The number of file permission bits on disk.
The number of CPU instructions executed per second.
The number of unique tag combinations, i.e., the number of series.
The number of columns in a SQL join.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

q: 为什么 user_id、request_id 这类高基数值通常不应该作为 TSDB tag？
q_en: Why should high-cardinality values like user_id or request_id usually not be TSDB tags?
options: 它们在写入时完全没办法被序列化成字节
它们会造出海量唯一 series，压垮内存索引并拖慢查询
它们的取值格式一定不允许是字符串类型
它们会导致所有数据的时间戳顺序颠倒
why: TSDB 会为每个唯一 tag 组合维护索引和元数据。把高基数值放 tag 会迅速耗尽内存，失去性能收益。
why_en: High-cardinality values like user IDs create too many series and can overwhelm the in-memory index.
options_en: They simply cannot be serialized into bytes when written.
They create massive numbers of unique series, overwhelming the in-memory index and slowing queries.
Their values are never allowed to be strings.
They cause every timestamp to be reversed in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个维度上唯一值组合的数量，这里指唯一 series 的数量。

scenario: 你必须随指标记录 request_id，但查询很少按 request_id 过滤。

q: 在 TSDB 中更适合把 request_id 放在哪里？
q_en: Where should request_id go in a TSDB?
options: 放 tag，因为所有字段都应该建索引
放 timestamp，替代原始采样时间
放 measurement name，让每个请求单独建一个 measurement
放 field，避免高基数 tag 造成 series 爆炸
why: 不常作为过滤条件的高基数值应作为 field 存储。这样仍能写入，但不会把 tag index 撑爆。
why_en: A rarely filtered high-cardinality value should be stored as a field rather than a tag.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个维度低基数且经常用于过滤，比如 region/env/service，放 tag 才能利用索引。
tradeoff: 放 field 换取可控 series 数量 vs 放 tag 换取可索引过滤
options_en: Put it in a tag, because every field should be indexed.
Put it in timestamp, replacing the original sample time.
Put it in measurement name, giving every request its own measurement.
Put it in a field, avoiding a high-cardinality tag that explodes the series count.

q: 补全 TSDB 的关键数据假设：
q_en: Complete the key TSDB data assumptions:
text: TSDB 的高性能依赖一些假设：tags 的 cardinality 较 {{low}}，采样时间较 {{regular}}，相邻数据点的 delta 较 {{small}}。
why: 这些假设让 tag index、时间压缩、value 压缩和时间分区都有效。一旦假设不成立，TSDB 可能比通用数据库更差。

q_en: For the target workload, what order of performance gain can a TSDB have over a general-purpose database?
options: 永远只快 1%，几乎感觉不到差别
永远慢 100x，专用系统反而更差

只影响 UI 展示，不影响存储或查询本身
why: 这个收益来自多种设计叠加：append-only、LSM、压缩、时间分区、Bloom filter、rollup 和 block pruning。前提是 workload 符合 TSDB 假设。

q: 是否应该因为数据带时间就默认上 TSDB？
q_en: Should you default to a TSDB just because the data has time?
options: 应该，只要数据字段里出现时间就必须优先考虑 TSDB
应该，因为 TSDB 能自动帮你处理所有排序和聚合逻辑

options_en: Yes, whenever a field contains time you must prioritize a TSDB.
Yes, because a TSDB automatically handles all sorting and aggregation logic for you.

scenario: 云监控平台持续接收 CPU、内存、磁盘、网络指标，用户主要看最近一小时/一周图表和告警。

q: 为什么 TSDB 比普通行式表更贴合？
q_en: Why does a TSDB fit better than a normal row table?

因为它针对追加写、时间分区、压缩和 rollup 做了专门优化
因为它的所有数据都只保存在内存里，完全不需要磁盘
因为它能自动理解业务含义，不需要工程师建模

q: TSDB 查询时为什么通常要同时看内存 buffer 和磁盘文件？
q_en: Why does a TSDB query usually check both the in-memory buffer and disk files?
options: 磁盘上的文件永远是空的，不会保存任何数据
内存 buffer 里只会缓存用户的头像图片
最新数据可能还在内存 buffer，较老数据已刷到磁盘

The in-memory buffer only caches user avatar images.
The newest data may still be in the in-memory buffer while older data has already been flushed to disk.
Checking both memory and disk is the only way to disable time filtering.

q: “writes are optimized to assist reads” 在 TSDB 里的意思更接近哪一个？

why_en: TSDB writes organize data by series and time so later reads touch fewer and more contiguous blocks.

Writes deliberately shuffle data out of order to make queries harder.
Writes keep only the last value per series and discard everything else.
Writes organize and compress data by series and time so later reads touch fewer, more sequential blocks.

q: 把“是否使用 TSDB”的决策链按顺序排列：
q_en: Put the "should we use a TSDB" decision chain in order:
steps: 如果这些假设不成立，回到 Postgres/DynamoDB/流处理等更通用方案
需要高吞吐追加写和按时间范围查询
选择 TSDB，并用时间分区、压缩、rollup 和 tag index 优化

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TSDB, or time-series database, is purpose-built for high-throughput append writes and time-range queries.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of unique tag combinations, i.e. the number of distinct series.

q: TSDB 的性能收益主要来自哪些可利用的数据特征？
q_en: What data features does a TSDB exploit for performance?
options: 时间天然有序，适合按窗口分区
同一 series 的相邻值和 timestamp 往往相似，适合压缩
每条数据都需要跨表强事务
查询常按低基数 tag 和时间范围裁剪
why: TSDB 是为特定形状的数据和查询设计的。强事务和复杂关系不是它的核心优势。
why_en: TSDBs gain performance by exploiting time order, compressible adjacent points, and low-cardinality tag filtering.
options_en: Time is naturally ordered, which fits windowed partitioning.
Adjacent values and timestamps within the same series tend to be similar, which compresses well.
Every point needs a strong cross-table transaction.
Queries are usually pruned by low-cardinality tags and a time range.
